properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 15 at 3:00PM EDT until October 16 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Blacksburg has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in North Carolina...

South Fork New River near Boone affecting Watauga County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...South Fork New River near Boone.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, water covers portions of Brookshire Road and
low-lying fields along the river. Area creeks and streams are running
high and could flood with more heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EDT Thursday the stage was 8.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.4 feet
early Friday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Friday
evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 15 at 3:00PM EDT until October 15 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
FFWRNK

The National Weather Service in Blacksburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Watauga County in northwestern North Carolina...

* Until 600 PM EDT.

* At 300 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Boone, Deerfield and Meat Camp.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 15 at 2:30PM EDT until October 15 at 6:30PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Haywood County in western North Carolina...

* Until 600 PM EDT.

* At 230 PM EDT, emergency management reported catastrophic flooding
along the Pigeon River in Canton. Water rescues are ongoing. Between
6 and 10 inches of rain have fallen.

This is a FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for Canton and Clyde. This is a
PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. Severe and
widespread flash flooding of homes, businesses, roads and bridges is
ongoing.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Canton, Clyde and Bethel.
properties.instruction:
This is a FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for the Pigeon River in Canton. SEEK
HIGHER GROUND NOW! Act quickly to protect your life. Do not attempt to
travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an
evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 15 at 2:00PM EDT until October 17 at 3:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of western North Carolina, including the
following counties, Avery, Buncombe, Haywood, Henderson, Madison,
Mitchell, Transylvania and Yancey, and the mountains of Burke,
Caldwell and McDowell.

* WHEN...From this evening through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Landslides
and debris flows are possible in steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Tropical moisture will bring 4 to 8 inches of rain to the
mountains, with locally higher amounts along the Blue Ridge
Escarpment.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
